Commentary.Commentary: England get the trophy and start celebrating. It was a superb effort from them throughout the series. They almost lost the first ODI but did well to tie and then Sri Lanka lost three games after that. That's it from us then! We have just one-off T20I left now and that will be played on 5th July at 1830 local time in Southampton. Let's see if Sri Lanka end the tour by winning that game at least. England will look to keep their unbeaten run in this tour. Do join us for that clash. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

EOIN MORGAN says it was a good toss to lose. Feels the fielding was a lot better and they adapted to the conditions quickly. Adds it was more of a sub-continent wicket today. He is proud of his players as they adapted really well and the bowlers stuck to their lengths. He feels it was an all-round performance. Feels the belief in the dressing room has been really good. Credits Jason Roy, Jos Buttler and Joe Root. He thinks the bowlers have picked wickets when they have required and have showed good skills. Adds they have grown together as a side as the series went on. Thinks it's a good chance to test new and fresh players in the one-off T20I game.

ANGELO MATHEWS says they have been having the same problems in batting, bowling and fielding. Credits England as they outplayed Sri Lanka. He feels the bowlers didn't hit the right areas. Adds it was a poor game overall for them. Mentions running was very poor in all the five games and they have to improve in a lot of areas. Credits England once again for the way they played throughout. He feels Sri Lanka went down after the first game which was tied. Says they are a young group. Adds the seniors have to play a major role and the youngsters have to grab every opportunity with both hands.

MAN OF THE SERIES, JASON ROY thinks he was getting 30s and 40s and it was a matter of time before he converted it. Adds he has put in a lot of hard work and credits the coaching staff. Rates Vince as a classy batsman. Says they have been playing as a team and they have to perform against Pakistan soon now. He says he wants to play Test cricket as well.

MAN OF THE MATCH, JOS BUTTLER says he has had good success against Sri Lanka and adds that's a fitting end to the series. He respects Jason Roy for playing so well throughout the series. Credits his teammates for putting a consistent performance. Mentions Root played a great innings today. Adds he has learned more and more and has gained more valuable experience. He says he is not focused on things which he can't control.
Time for presentation. The match officials get their medals.

The English bowlers and fielders take great credit for this feat since they were primarily responsible for dismantling the batsmen. Willey was the master wicket-taker amongst the bowlers, with four scalps in his kitty and an economy rate of below 4. Running second was Plunkett with three wickets to his name, followed by Rashid and his brace.

Three down, Chandimal came in and held his end of the line for nearly the rest of the innings but the other batsmen were not able to sustain things at their end for long. Sri Lanka lost wickets thick and fast and were plagued with a lack of runs to add to it.

The early wicket of Perera and Gunathilaka's start foretold their impending fall but it was held at bay by the firm partnership between Mendis and Gunathilaka. Mendis' wicket, taken down by a well-aimed throw from Bairstow, heralded the beginning of the end for the Sri Lankans.

The Englishmen continue their winning streak after winning another one-sided game! The visitors faced a difficult target of 325 but the strength of their batting line-up was never in question. However, when they took the field, another story was told.
